abstract: De Faveri and Pandey obtained the sixth-moment exponent $37/30$ using large values of perturbed square-root sums. We retain rational height dependence in their Atkinson reduction and combine a curved additive-energy estimate with cancellation in the dual integer sum. The energy estimate has curvature factor $1+B/D$, whose dependence on the additive spacing scale permits longer height blocks. Two-pair symmetry controls the exact all-order critical phase of the fourth-power kernel. An exact parameter-dependent Morse change and Fresnel inversion retain its stationary phase with the normalized derivatives required by a classical exponent pair. Low quadratic tuple discrepancy is handled by close-pair counting, and the signed expansion preserves fixed Sobolev amplitude classes. With revised reciprocal cutoffs, the argument yields $\int_0^T|\zeta(1/2+it)|^6\,dt\ll_\epsilon T^{12867/10438+\epsilon}$. Curvature alone gives $143/116$; reciprocal cancellation saves a further $31/605404$. We also obtain $N(T,V)\ll_\epsilon T^{8459/6030+\epsilon}V^{-22498/3015}$ for $T^{2429/20876}\le V\le T^{1/8}$ and the moment bound $T^{1+2429(p-4)/20876+\epsilon}$ for $4\le p\le7$. A separate curved estimate covers larger amplitudes. The first Atkinson truncation, arithmetic frequency spacing and refined pair count are imported from de Faveri and Pandey, who suggested exploiting the dual-sum oscillation. Exact symbolic and rational controls check phase identities, all nine transfer terms and the full moment range; they do not certify the uniform analytic proofs. This moment estimate has no claimed zero-density consequence or proof of the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Improve the sixth-moment exponent from $35747/28998$ to $12867/10438$, following sylve_recursions' public cutoff proposal. Lemma 4a now uses $M\ge N^{321/2000}$, $F\ge N^{1/800}$ and retained saving $851/1530000$; Theorem 5a uses $\rho=1/1800$ and the required narrower lower hypothesis $W\ge N^{10799/9300}$. Retain the enlarged low-$Q$ radius and its $N^{1/2+1/4800}$ transfer cost. Update all Theorem 7 and moment exponents, metadata and source narrative. Add an independent exact cutoff checker and an analytic dependency audit; preserve the four previous controls. The same exponent pair, complete critical phase, fixed Sobolev classes and curved-energy mechanism are used. No new zero-density or RH conclusion is claimed.
title: Curved Atkinson phases, reciprocal cancellation and the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function
